card: Uses mocktime in functional test p2p_tx_privacy.py to avoid flakiness from unbounded random inbound transaction announcement delays. The test previously relied on a 60-second real-time timeout, causing sporadic failures when Poisson delays exceeded the threshold. The author verified that advancing mocktime resolves a forced 12-minute delay in 1 second while maintaining regression detection. Addresses an instance of timeout flakiness tracked under issue #19732.
changed_since_previous: Diff provided for the first time (+7 lines in test/functional/p2p_tx_privacy.py). No structural changes to the logic.
evidence: Addresses part of tracking issue #19732 on functional tests vulnerable to timeouts.

Author verification notes that with the reproduction patch forcing a 12-minute delay, master fails at 60s while this patch passes in 1s, and removing the net_processing guard still catches the regression.
problem: In p2p_tx_privacy.py, the test relies on real time while waiting for an inv announcement subject to a random unbounded inbound delay. An unlucky draw can exceed the 60-second test timeout and cause intermittent test failures.

risk.why: Only touches a single functional test file by adding mocktime controls.

summary: Freezes mocktime before peers connect in p2p_tx_privacy.py and advances it by 3600 seconds after sending the second transaction. This triggers the node's queued transaction announcements deterministically without relying on real-time Poisson delays.
